assessmentQuestions.question: You are designing a high-throughput notification dispatch engine for 50 million active users. Peak load reaches 120,000 push messages per second. Which architecture ensures lowest latency and prevents downstream APNs/FCM rate-limit cascading failures?
assessmentQuestions.codeSnippet:
// Proposed Architecture flow:
API Gateway -> [?] -> Worker Consumer Pool -> Circuit Breaker -> Apple/Google Push

options.text: Synchronous REST calls directly from API Gateway with exponential thread pools
Distributed Message Broker (Kafka / RabbitMQ) with Token Bucket rate limiters & Dead Letter Queues (DLQs)
Single relational SQL database queue polled via cron job every 5 seconds
Redis PUB/SUB without persistent log storage or backpressure buffering

assessmentQuestions.explanation: Distributed message queues (Kafka) paired with partitioned consumer groups and token-bucket circuit breakers decouple high-velocity ingestion from third-party vendor rate limits while guaranteeing at-least-once delivery.

assessmentQuestions.question: In a React 18 / Next.js application experiencing laggy re-renders during high-frequency real-time stock ticker updates, which optimization delivers the best UX without unnecessary CPU cycles?

options.text: Wrap every single JSX element in React.memo and disable strict mode
Use useTransition or useDeferredValue combined with selective state sub-slices (Zustand / signals)
Force all updates through document.getElementById manipulation in useEffect
Store ticker feed in global Redux store without reselect memoization

assessmentQuestions.explanation: React 18 concurrent features (useTransition/useDeferredValue) allow critical UI interactions (clicks, scrolling) to interrupt background ticker render updates, preventing thread starvation.

assessmentQuestions.question: When deploying a multi-region containerized microservice on Kubernetes requiring zero-downtime rollouts and canary traffic splitting (90% stable, 10% canary), which strategy is industry standard?

options.text: Recreate deployment strategy where old pods are killed simultaneously before new ones start
Service Mesh (Istio/Linkerd) or Argo Rollouts using automated metric analysis (error rates, p99 latency)
Manually altering DNS A-records in Route53 with 60-second TTLs during maintenance hours
SSH into each node and run docker run -p 80:80 latest_image

assessmentQuestions.explanation: Argo Rollouts and modern Service Meshes provide progressive delivery with automated canary analysis that rolls back instantaneously if error thresholds or latency SLIs breach safe limits.

assessmentQuestions.question: You need to find the Top-K most frequently searched keywords across a streaming log of billions of search queries with constrained memory (O(K) space complexity). Which data structure combination is most optimal?

options.text: Sort the entire array of queries in-place using Quicksort O(N log N)
Count-Min Sketch probabilistic frequency estimator coupled with a Min-Heap of size K
Nested For-Loops with an adjacency matrix
Binary Search Tree storing every distinct string in memory

assessmentQuestions.explanation: Count-Min Sketch provides bounded probabilistic frequency estimates in sub-linear space, while a Min-Heap of size K efficiently maintains the top elements in O(log K) insertion time.

assessmentQuestions.question: When implementing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline on proprietary technical manuals, users complain about vague answers for specific API parameters. What technique best mitigates this?

options.text: Increase the LLM temperature to 1.0 to encourage creativity
Hybrid Search (BM25 keyword search + Dense Vector embedding) with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and Cohere re-ranking
Feed the entire 50,000-page PDF into a single system prompt
Disable vector embeddings and use simple string.includes()

assessmentQuestions.explanation: Hybrid search combines exact lexical matching (essential for API names, acronyms, and error codes) with semantic vector search, followed by cross-encoder re-ranking for pinpoint accuracy.

assessmentQuestions.question: During a cross-functional sprint, an industry product manager introduces a critical requirement change 2 days before release that threatens the team SLA. What is the most constructive response?

options.text: Ignore the message and deploy the original code silently
Quantify trade-offs with data, propose a phased scope (MVP for deadline + Phase 2 patch), and align all stakeholders transparently
Complain publicly in the all-hands channel about lack of planning
Accept without questions and work 48 hours without sleep to deliver low-quality code

assessmentQuestions.explanation: High-performing engineers present objective impact assessments, offer viable compromise paths (phased rollouts), and establish clear alignment without compromising system stability.
